text:
lia: heads-up — we need to finalize the key-rotation window for customer envelope keys. thinking about automatic monthly rotation vs manual-triggered rewrap. concerns about client compatibility and audit trails.
jonas: +1. timeline? we should avoid high-traffic hours for bulk rewrap.
maria: also need to plan RBAC changes — the rewrap worker needs kms:Encrypt kms:Decrypt + a temporary role that is audited. no long-lived keys for that role.
alex: agree. for cloud providers we need separate perms: AWS kms:ReEncrypt, GCP cryptoKeys.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt, Azure unwrapKey/wrapKey. document these in the runbook.
samir: one more: how do we handle old envelope headers? some long-tail clients still read legacy header v1. runtime should accept v1 and v2 for at least 3 weeks post-rollout.
lia: proposal: canary for 5% of customers first day, 25% next 3 days, then full — with automatic rollback if >0.5% error rate in decoding.
jonas: telemetry: emit metric rewrap.failures per key_version and envelope_version. add trace id correlation so we can tie to request IDs.
maria: audit logging: every rewrap action must log actor, source IP, key id, old_key_version, new_key_version, item_count and a sha256 of ciphertext (not plaintext). retention 1 year for compliance.
alex: for manual-triggered rewraps we should have a dry-run flag: `--dry-run --limit 1000` to validate without changing stored ciphertext. sample command in ops repo: `./tools/rewrap --project redwood-prod --key target-kms --dry-run --limit 1000`. put it behind a protected route in the console.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled job window created: 2024-11-12T01:00Z — 2024-11-12T05:00Z (UTC) for canary.
samir: vuln-triage note: if we discover a key compromise mid-rollout, the plan must switch to emergency rotate + revoke old signing keys and invalidate all caches. need runbook steps for rollback and customer notification.
lia: question about fallback: should runtime fail-open to serve cached plaintext if rewrap fails? I'm leaning no — fail closed and surface 503 with explanation. we can enable emergency bypass mode for verified SRE ops only.
jonas: +1, fail-open has data-exposure risk. provide clear retry/backoff to clients and a status page incident banner.
maria: RBAC change schedule: create feature branch with Terraform diff, run internal audit preview, then apply in a staged manner with PR gating. link to terraform plan: https://git.internal/plan/rotations-172345.
alex: don't forget to validate cross-cloud KMS latency. rewrap is network-bound for some keys; add a worker with exponential backoff and per-key concurrency limits.
lia: ok next steps: 1) finalize runbook doc and RBAC terraform diff (owners: maria/alex) 2) add telemetry + dry-run tooling (owners: jonas/samir) 3) schedule canary during low-traffic window and notif ENG/SEC/CS. target canary date: 2024-11-12.
samir: I'll open a short incident-prep checklist for CS and security comms.
alex: I'll add the provider-specific permission table to the runbook.
lia: thanks — tagging @maria @jonas for follow-up. I’ll update the SLO playbook with the rollback thresholds. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: note: make sure to create an audit log retention snapshot before the canary start.
